originalFinding.kind: learning visibility concern in principal physical demonstration
originalFinding.description: The horse-pulling demonstration changes to a distant composition dominated by empty wall and desk. The joined copper sphere itself is only about one tenth of the portrait width, with small horse legs, a thin joint line, and a tiny valve. The ensemble fits, but the critical physical evidence—pulling effort while the two halves remain joined—is much less legible than in the preceding hemisphere close view.
originalFinding.fullFrameCheck: Original 1080×1920 frames at 337.0 s and 338.5 s still allow four horses on each side, outward-facing pull direction, taut ropes, and a closed seam to be identified. This is a visibility/teaching-strength concern, not a claim that the count, direction, or closed state is wrong, and not a claim that animation is absent.
originalFinding.learningImpact: A viewer must inspect a small joint and small leg movement to connect the horses' force with the failure to separate; an overall group-width proxy does not establish readability of those critical features.
originalFinding.proposedInScopeRemedyForParent: Consider a closer view or tighter physical arrangement that keeps all eight horses and the hemisphere joint readable during the pulling explanation. Reinspect the actual final encoded result if changed. No changes performed by this reviewer.
originalFinding.motionLimit: Contact-sheet cells and two static full frames do not prove or disprove continuous leg animation. Any stronger conclusion about the pull animation needs playback or additional motion review outside this assigned static scope.
